instruction.text: First, read this online article about Easter Island. Then, answer the questions.

atoms.text: Easter Island is located in the Pacific Ocean more than 2,200 miles from Chile. It is one of the most remote islands on Earth that is still inhabited. Easter Island has a triangular shape and is formed from three dormant volcanoes. Scientists estimate that the island was first populated by the Rapa Nui people more than 3,000 years ago, and to this day, the island is home to their descendants. Easter Island is world-famous for its more than 900 stone statues that were erected across the whole island.

hint.text: A dormant volcano is a volcano that is currently not active but is likely to erupt in the future again.
hint.label: Dormant volcano

atoms.text: The traditional name for the statues is moai which loosely translates to 'stone statue'. Most of the moai are more than 500 years old and have been carved out of soft volcanic stone by the Rapa Nui people. Each one of the statues was carved from a single block of stone and then moved across the island to its final destination. Scientists believe that the statues were built to honour and represent deified ancestors or other important people of the island. To this day, it is unclear how the Rapa Nui people moved these massive statues across the island. However, traditional stories, passed down through generations of the Rapa Nui people, claim that the statues 'walked' to their chosen destination. The moai are very holy and powerful stone statues and a symbol of the highly developed culture of the Rapa Nui people.

hint.text: Deified means to make someone or something god-like.
hint.label: Deified

atoms.text: This picture shows two moai buried in dirt up to their chest.
Here you can see 8 moai standing in a row next to each other facing inland. The tallest moai on Easter Island is 33 feet tall and weighs more than 82 tons.

instruction.text: Look at the pictures. Which facts are true about Easter Island and the moai? Select the correct statements.

b.sound: There are many trees on Easter Island.
All moai stand on the shore of the Island.
Most moai are standing upright, but some have tipped over and lie on the ground.
The moai standing at the shore are turning their backs to the water and look inland.
All moai are wearing a hat-like, stone piece on their heads.
The moai don’t show any signs of weathering.

hint.text: Weathering means that material is slowly damaged and worn out by the force of rain, wind or waves.
hint.label: Weathering

correct.text: The second photo shows what the moai looked like when they were first erected. Eyes were painted onto their faces, and they wore big red cylinders on their heads. Over time, wind and rain caused weathering and slowly damaged the moai.
